items.label: text
items.text: If you plot a graph of [NzOs] against time using the above data, you will find that the line is curved and the half-life is constant; as a result, the reaction is first order with respect to NOs.

items.label: text
items.text: The rate of reaction at any given time canbe determined from a concentration-time or volume-time graphby drawing a tangent to the curve at the given time and calculating the gradient of the tangent.

items.label: text
items.text: A tangent to the curve has been drawn at time = 400 s.

items.label: text
items.text: To find the rate at this time point, draw as large a triangle as possible and then measure x and y.

items.label: text
items.text: x= 1470 s and y = -1.60 mol dm-3.

items.label: formula
items.text:
rate = − change in concentration of reactant / time
= − (−1.60 mol dm⁻³ / 1470 s) = 1.09 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹

items.label: text
items.text: The procedure is exactly the same for a volume-time graph for a gas evolved (Section 11A.1) This time the curve will slope upwards not downwards (fig D).
